search_space: Exhaustively swept all 626 triples (A,B,ω) for uniform finite spaces Ω={0,...,n-1} with 1≤n≤4, where A is any subset of Ω, B is any nonempty subset of Ω, and ω∈B represents an observed outcome for which B is known to have occurred.
witness_description: In the uniform probability space Ω={0,1}, take A=B={0} and suppose the observed outcome is 0, so B is known to have occurred. Then Pr(A given B)=1, while Pr(A ∩ B)=1/2.
refutation_explanation: The two exact probabilities differ: 1 is not equal to 1/2. Thus knowing that B occurred does not make the conditional probability equal to the original, unconditional probability of A ∩ B.
